data: Carbonaceous near-Earth asteroid sampled by OSIRIS-REx. The spacecraft collected a regolith sample in October 2020 and returned it to Earth in September 2023 — the first US asteroid sample-return. Bennu is a hydrated, carbon-rich rubble pile and a probable past parent body for primitive meteorites.
OSIRIS-REx — NASA, 2018–21 (orbital survey + Touch-and-Go sample collection)
OSIRIS-APEX (extended mission) — NASA, en route to Apophis 2029
Bennu is a near-Earth asteroid (semi-major axis 1.13 AU) — close enough that OSIRIS-REx could rendezvous, sample, and return material to Earth in 7 years.
Bennu's 0.204 eccentricity gives it a low probability impact path with Earth in the 2100s — one of the reasons it was chosen for OSIRIS-REx (planetary-defence reconnaissance).
Half the longest diameter of the orbit ellipse — and the single number that sets the orbital period.
How stretched the orbit is — zero is a perfect circle, one is a parabolic escape.
